In 0.52.1 the `directory=...` constructor still forwards `**env_options` (including `autoescape=True`) into `jinja2.Environment(**env_options)`, but does so through a path the library itself flags with `warnings.warn('Extra environment options are deprecated. In 1.3.1 that kwarg-forwarding is removed entirely; `Jinja2Templates.__init__` no longer accepts `autoescape` for the directory path at all (it hardcodes `jinja2.select_autoescape()`), so this exact call would raise `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'autoescape'` at import time. fastapi (and therefore starlette) is unpinned in pyproject.toml, so a future `uv lock --upgrade` could pull a version where this call breaks. Today, under the locked 0.52.1, autoescape remains True and no live XSS path exists; the control now simply depends on a deprecated, version-fragile forwarding path rather than an unconditionally-constructed Environment.

Making that single control depend on a path the framework has already marked deprecated means a routine, unrelated dependency bump could silently change or break how escaping is configured. The one newer starlette version checked fails loudly (TypeError at startup) rather than silently disabling escaping, so the immediate risk is low, but no evidence rules out an intermediate version where the extra kwarg is silently dropped instead of raised/warned.

findings.problem: This diff reverts commit e11187e ("fix: use preconfigured jinja2.Environment for autoescape"), whose message states plainly: "Starlette removed the **env_options passthrough in Jinja2Templates, breaking autoescape=True on newer versions." I read the actual installed Starlette in this project's venv (.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/templating.py) and confirmed `Jinja2Templates.__init__` only accepts `directory`, `context_processors`, and `env` — there is no `**env_options` passthrough and no `autoescape` parameter. Calling `Jinja2Templates(directory=str(TEMPLATES_DIR), autoescape=True)` therefore raises `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'autoescape'` immediately, and since `templates = Jinja2Templates(...)` executes at module scope, importing `triggarr.web.routes` fails and the app cannot start.
findings.title: Jinja2Templates(autoescape=True) kwarg is unsupported by the installed Starlette and will raise TypeError at import time
findings.why_it_matters: Every route in this router (the whole dashboard/config UI) becomes unreachable because the module fails to import — this is a guaranteed, reproducible startup crash, not a latent edge case. It also undoes a documented, intentional fix for autoescape, which CLAUDE.md calls out explicitly ("in Jinja2, never ... disable autoescaping"); on a hypothetical Starlette version that silently tolerated the extra kwarg instead of raising, this same change would quietly disable autoescape and reopen template-injection/XSS risk.

findings.problem: The explicit Jinja environment is replaced with Starlette's deprecated **env_options path. [Starlette 0.52.1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kludex/starlette/0.52.1/starlette/templating.py) forwards autoescape=True today (lines 85–108), so this is not a current XSS bypass. However, the escaping guarantee now depends on that deprecated forwarding behavior. Dockerfile installs unbounded dependencies from pyproject.toml without uv.lock. If forwarding lapses and escaping defaults change, a movie title such as flows through search/engine.py:401–402, db.py:367, and templates/partials/search_log.html:19 into executable HTML. Removal of the keyword could instead prevent application startup.
